principles.text: Build around core human desires like attraction, status and self-improvement, not an over-intellectualized use case.
Pick creators by engaged comment sections and views, not follower counts, and DM hundreds of them a day.
Test many hooks and angles, then double down hard on whatever returns a profit on time or money invested.
Ship a bad first version fast. The worst failure is not shipping bad code, it is shipping nothing.
When a copycat appears, go all in on distribution right away instead of waiting to perfect the product.

sampleQA.question: How do I know if an influencer promo is worth paying for?

answer.text: A promo is profitable when revenue per thousand views, after variable costs, beats the cost per thousand views.
Pay for views and engagement, not follower counts.
Look at comment sections: thoughtful, liked replies signal trust and conversion, fire emojis do not.
Most creators lose money, but a few return 10x. Find those and run as many of them as you can.

sampleQA.question: Should I raise VC for my consumer app?

answer.text: In consumer apps cash is not the bottleneck; industry insight and agency are, so bootstrapping works.
If you want to make millions, don't raise. If you want a chance at billions, raise.
Being profitable means you are not beholden to VCs who can block your decisions.
The downside: every dollar you spend comes out of your own pocket.

sampleQA.question: How should I price my app's subscription?

answer.text: Let the channel set the price: paid ads suit higher prices, organic suits lower ones like $30 a year or $4 a week.
Split-test offers and placements with a paywall tool; it can take revenue per download to 1.5x or 2x.
He accepts a lower LTV per download in exchange for more users and more word of mouth.
